title: Nine Things She Said
scopeNote: This keeps the nine fixed statements and the framework switch that recodes every one of them, cut from seven frameworks to five. The account-matching task and the side-by-side framework comparison stay in the longer version. The output here is coverage rather than a ranking, which is what distinguishes it from the paired activity on power.
summary: Five frameworks for the self applied to the same nine statements. Each makes exactly two central and has no concept at all for at least two, and one statement is central to none of them.
learningObjectives: Say which question each framework for the self asks.
Explain why what a framework makes central is inseparable from what it cannot represent.
Recognise that having no concept for something is not the same as denying it.
Identify the statement no framework here treats as its own business.
Explain why a framework that could represent everything would predict nothing.
interactionTypes: a framework switch that recodes all nine
counts of what each framework can and cannot represent
a coverage tracker across the frameworks tried
a five-by-nine summary table revealing the statement nobody claims
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. Nothing is asked about the reader and no score is produced for anybody.
dataStatus: Nadia is invented and the nine statements were written for teaching. The codings are authored judgements, the page says so, and a good argument for a different coding should be credited.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout. The framework is a group of native radio buttons in a labelled fieldset. Every coding is given in words in a real table with row and column headers, and rows carry a non-colour state attribute as reinforcement rather than as the signal. The framework's question appears as text in a notice rather than only as a heading, and the coverage tracker and the summary verdict are both stated in words. Nothing is timed and there is no motion.
simulationNotes: Each framework carries, for each of the nine statements, one of three codings: central, usable, or no concept for it. The structure is arranged rather than incidental and every part of it is verified in the test suite. Each of the five frameworks treats exactly two statements as central, so none is presented as covering more ground than another; each has no concept at all for at least two; eight of the nine statements are central to at least one framework; and the ninth, where the fees went up and the hours were cut, is central to none of them and reachable by exactly one, indirectly. Five frameworks rather than seven is what makes that last claim clean. Possible selves and self-efficacy are cut, and possible selves is one of the two frameworks in the original that codes the September statement as usable; keeping both would have blunted the point, and keeping one leaves it reachable rather than untouchable, which is the more honest version. One observation about the original, whose data is untouched by anything here: its header comment states that the September statement is coded as having no concept by six of its seven frameworks and as usable by the seventh, while its own data has two frameworks coding it usable. The discrepancy is in the comment rather than in the data.
readmeTopic: why every framework for the self has something it cannot see
